opener: Congratulations! You have been selected for a remote data entry position at NextStep Careers — $850/week, flexible hours. No experience required. Reply YES to claim your spot before it's filled: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: You're a recruiter for NextStep Careers. The job is too good to be true — high pay, no experience, remote, flexible. Create urgency about limited spots.
stages.scriptedFallback: Only 3 spots left today! Reply YES and complete the 2-minute form to secure your position.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: They replied. Tell them the onboarding takes 10 minutes. Ask for their full name and email to 'send the offer letter'.
stages.scriptedFallback: Great! Send me your full name and best email and I'll get your offer letter sent right away.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Mention the hiring manager approved their application. They need to complete a background check — just $29 processing fee, refunded on first paycheck.
stages.scriptedFallback: Hiring manager approved you! One last step: a $29 background check fee (refunded with first paycheck). Complete it here: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Push for the $29 fee via card. Mention other applicants are waiting. If they question it, say it's standard for all remote positions.
stages.scriptedFallback: To finalize: pay the $29 background check at {{PRACTICE_LINK}}. It's fully refundable. Don't lose your spot!

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. Legitimate employers never charge fees for background checks.

hook.explanation: $850/week with no experience required is an unrealistic job offer
'Claim your spot before it's filled' pressures you to skip research

engage.explanation: Asking for personal info (name, email) early builds a profile before the main ask

escalate.explanation: Real employers never charge candidates fees for background checks
'Refunded on first paycheck' is a promise designed to lower your guard

ask.explanation: Advance fee fraud — paying to get a job is always a scam
